title: Caesar Cipher
problem: Read a whole number k on the first line, then a text of lower-case letters and spaces on the second line. Shift every letter k places forward in the alphabet, wrapping around from z back to a, and leave the spaces unchanged. Print the result. For example, 3 and abc xyz gives def abc.
starter_code:
# Line 1: the shift k. Line 2: text of lower-case letters and spaces.
# Print the text with every letter shifted k places forward (z wraps to a).

# Write your code here

hints.1: Each letter has a position in the alphabet, from 0 for a to 25 for z. Think about shifting the position and then turning it back into a letter.
hints.2: Turn a letter into its position with ord(letter) - ord("a"), add k, and use % 26 to wrap around. chr() turns a number back into a character. Spaces must be copied as they are, and k can be larger than 26.

failure_explanation: Work with the letter's position in the alphabet and wrap it with the remainder after dividing by 26, so that z goes back to a and a shift larger than 26 still works. Spaces are not letters and must be copied unchanged, and a shift of zero must leave the text exactly as it was.
